title: LedgerEvent
description: One event in a project's append-only ledger (spec §5-P2, §6). Every state change in the platform is exactly one of these, committed by the Arbiter. Payload object shapes are governed per type; objects marked 'see claim.schema.json' etc. are enforced by convention in v1.0. `format` keywords are assertions. v1.2 adds three event types (session.status_changed, finding.raised, finding.resolved) and optional fields; every v1.1 event is a valid v1.2 event.

seq.description: Per-project monotonic commit order, stamped by the Arbiter.

prev_hash.description: Hash chain for tamper evidence, stamped by the Arbiter. Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the previous committed event in the same project (the one with seq - 1), computed over that event's canonical JSON: the whole event object as committed, its own prev_hash included, with keys sorted, separators ',' and ':', non-ASCII characters not escaped, encoded as UTF-8. The first event of a project (seq 0) has no predecessor and omits the field.

proposal_id.description: Unique within the project across claim proposals and model patch proposals, which share one namespace. Arbiter-enforced.

from_proposal.description: The proposal_id of a committed claim.proposed event in the same project. Arbiter-enforced.

cause_event.description: The verification, waiver, or refutation event id that justifies the move (§7 promotion rules).

ModelPatchProposed.description: A proposed patch is held to the rules of a committed one (Arbiter-enforced): base_version must be the head of its branch (BASE_MOVED when the branch's head has moved on; v1.2: BASE_NOT_BRANCH_HEAD when the base is not a version of that branch), every update_element or remove_element target must exist in the head's model (PATCH_TARGET_MISSING), and the model the patch would produce must validate against system_model.schema.json (INVALID_MODEL_RESULT).

proposal_id.description: Unique within the project across claim proposals and model patch proposals, which share one namespace. Arbiter-enforced.

branch.description: v1.2: the model branch this event belongs to. Absent means "main", so a ledger without the field means exactly what it meant under v1.1.

ModelPatchCommitted.description: Commits version_id as the model that applying patch to base_version's model produces, and makes it the head of its branch. Arbiter-enforced: base_version is the head of the branch (BASE_MOVED when the branch's head has moved on; v1.2: BASE_NOT_BRANCH_HEAD when the base is not a version of that branch); every update_element or remove_element target exists (PATCH_TARGET_MISSING); the resulting model validates against system_model.schema.json (INVALID_MODEL_RESULT); version_id was never used in the project (DUPLICATE_VERSION_ID).

from_proposal.description: The proposal_id of a committed model.patch_proposed event in the same project. Arbiter-enforced.

branch.description: v1.2: the model branch this event belongs to. Absent means "main", so a ledger without the field means exactly what it meant under v1.1.

ModelVersionCreated.description: Creates a model version and makes it the head of its branch. Without `parent` it is the genesis version, allowed only while the project has no model version at all (DUPLICATE_GENESIS when its branch already has a head; v1.2: BRANCH_NEEDS_PARENT when another branch does). With `parent` it must name a model version already committed in the same project, on any branch (UNKNOWN_MODEL_VERSION), and the new version's model is a copy of the parent's (v1.1, P-7). version_id must not have been used in the project (DUPLICATE_VERSION_ID). All Arbiter-enforced. v1.2: a project has one head per branch; a branch begins with a model.version_created that names it and a committed parent.

parent.description: A model version already committed in the same project (by model.version_created or model.patch_committed), on any branch.

branch.description: v1.2: the model branch this event belongs to. Absent means "main", so a ledger without the field means exactly what it meant under v1.1.

objection.description: Conforms to the Objection body in agent_protocol.schema.json.

ref.description: The patch, waiver, or check that resolves it.

signer.description: Human id; §5-P11 — waivers are signed human events.

model_version.description: v1.1: the model version the result judges.

as_of_seq.description: v1.1: the project's knowledge (claims, waivers) the check ran against: everything committed up to this seq.

round.description: v1.2: the session's round when it entered the phase (0 before the loop).

package_ref.description: v1.2: the content hash of the session package written so far, if any.

SessionStatusChanged.description: v1.2 (P-11): a session's status changed, or a human's decision at a gate was refused. With session.phase_changed, session.checkpoint, budget.updated and waiver.signed it makes a session's whole story replayable from the ledger: the session read model is a projection. Arbiter-enforced: an event whose decision is approve, approve_with_risks or reject must come from a human actor (DECISION_NOT_HUMAN).

status.description: The status the session is in after this event: running, paused, awaiting_approval, approved, approved_with_risks, rejected, cancelled, failed, or an outcome the session ended in without a gate.

outcome.description: How the design loop ended: completed, completed_with_risks, stopped_budget, stopped_time, cancelled, failed.

decision.description: The decision taken at a human gate that caused this change (or, with refused, that was asked for).

reason.description: Why: the human's reason for approve_with_risks, the cause of a failure, the convergence rule's stop reason, or why a decision was refused.

package_ref.description: The content hash of the session package this status refers to.

refused.description: true: the decision was asked for and NOT applied; status is the unchanged current status and reason says why.

gate_verdict.description: The gate verdict of the package the session waits on or ended with.

preset.description: On the session's first event: the preset it runs under.

limits.description: The session's resolved limits: on its first event, and again when an extend decision raises them.

brief_source_id.description: On the session's first event: the source the brief was ingested as.

FindingRaised.description: v1.2 (P-12): a discovery finding: a question, a risk or a hypothesis a detector raises about the project's knowledge or model. A finding is never a fact: it is not a claim and nothing may cite it as evidence. Arbiter-enforced: every ref resolves to a committed claim, source, model version, decision, model element or entity of the project (UNKNOWN_REF); every evidence claim is committed (UNKNOWN_CLAIM); finding_id was never used (DUPLICATE_FINDING_ID); no OPEN finding has the same dedupe_key (DUPLICATE_FINDING).

refs.description: What the finding is about: ids of claims, entities, model elements, sources, decisions or model versions.

evidence_claims.description: The committed claims the detector read to raise it.

dedupe_key.description: Stable across runs for the same finding: a detector that sees the same thing again raises nothing new.

FindingResolved.description: v1.2 (P-12): closes an open finding (FINDING_NOT_OPEN otherwise, Arbiter-enforced).

ref.description: What resolves it: a claim, an experiment, a waiver, an objection, a model version.
